rationale: The candidate is a coherent simple ring-like box in all four views, so it passes basic solidity and repair integrity, but it is not a convincing neighborhood-living massing yet. The dominant gesture is readable, and the central void is legible from top and oblique views, but the overall expression is too generic and box-like relative to the brief. More importantly, the road frontage/access edge is not resolved as an active public threshold: the building reads as a sealed object with no clear front-side carve, notch, or entry seam aligned to the verified access edge. The form also fails program fit because neighborhood living here asks for a compact street building with active ground edge, one clear public void or terrace, and calm upper massing; this candidate’s roof/section logic is just a shallow hollowed extrusion, closer to an object with an atrium than a responsive mixed-use street building. It is therefore not program-fit hard-pass. A transferable correction would be to preserve the compact ring anchor but open or notch the access side of the courtyard and slightly deepen the void so the ground threshold becomes legible.
